title: Quiz: Comparing Aerobic and Anaerobic Respiration

questions.stem: Which type of respiration produces more ATP per glucose molecule?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration produces approximately 38 ATP per glucose molecule, while anaerobic respiration produces only 2 ATP. Aerobic is much more efficient because glucose is completely oxidised.

questions.stem: Which type of respiration requires oxygen?
questions.explanation: Only aerobic respiration requires oxygen. Anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen, which is why it is used during intense exercise when oxygen supply is insufficient.

questions.stem: What are the products of anaerobic respiration in animals?
questions.explanation: In animal cells, anaerobic respiration produces only lactic acid. Unlike in yeast, no carbon dioxide is produced during anaerobic respiration in animal cells.

questions.stem: In which part of the cell does anaerobic respiration occur?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration occurs in the cytoplasm only. It does not involve the mitochondria. Aerobic respiration starts in the cytoplasm but is completed in the mitochondria.

questions.stem: Why might a sprinter rely more on anaerobic respiration than a marathon runner?

options.text: Sprinting requires rapid energy release, faster than aerobic respiration can supply

questions.explanation: Sprinting requires a very rapid burst of energy that aerobic respiration alone cannot supply fast enough. Anaerobic respiration provides additional ATP quickly, though at the cost of lactic acid build-up.

questions.stem: What is a disadvantage of anaerobic respiration in muscles?

options.text: Lactic acid builds up, causing muscle fatigue and cramps

questions.explanation: Lactic acid produced during anaerobic respiration accumulates in muscles, lowering pH and causing fatigue, pain, and cramps. This limits how long intense exercise can be maintained.

questions.stem: Which statement is true about both aerobic and anaerobic respiration?

options.text: Both break down glucose to release energy

questions.explanation: Both aerobic and anaerobic respiration break down glucose molecules to release energy in the form of ATP. This is their fundamental shared purpose, though they differ in efficiency and products.
